summary: Metering imbalance during ephemeral agent fanout causing intermittent 429 responses
description: Issue summary: Customer reports periodic spikes of 429 responses for background ingest jobs immediately after a release of a sidecar orchestrator. Impact: Background pipeline (bulk embeddings) sees 10-15% request failures for ~5-10 minutes; interactive traffic unaffected but customer sees requeue/backoff failures in their orchestrated workers. Environment: Dedicated pool in prod-us-west, private VPC peered with AtlasData. Suspected area: token accounting / proxy fanout interaction with ephemeral workers and healthcheck/heartbeat requests.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy orchestrator sidecar with ephemeral worker pool enabled (replica factor 8).
2) Kick off bulk embedding job (concurrent worker count ~120).
3) Observe burst of small keepalive/heartbeat requests from ephemeral agents to control plane.
4) After ~30-90s, many client requests begin to receive 429 from rate-limiter for tenant namespace.
5) When ephemeral pool reduces, 429s stop within ~5-10 minutes.
logs:
Excerpt from nginx edge (prod-us-west) showing early 429s:
[2026-03-12T17:21:03Z] atlasdata/worker-42 POST /v1/embeddings 200 128ms
[2026-03-12T17:21:04Z] atlasdata/ephemeral-heartbeat GET /health 204 5ms
[2026-03-12T17:21:04Z] atlasdata/worker-43 POST /v1/embeddings 429 3ms x-rate-reason=tenant_quota_exhausted
[2026-03-12T17:21:05Z] atlasdata/ephemeral-heartbeat GET /health 204 4ms
[2026-03-12T17:21:05Z] atlasdata/worker-44 POST /v1/embeddings 429 2ms x-rate-reason=tenant_quota_exhausted
(Full logs uploaded to support bundle: s3://redwood-support-bundles/SUP-575575/2026-03-12.tar.gz)
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: heartbeats from ephemeral agents were being attributed to the same tenant token bucket as embedding requests because healthcheck path was not excluded by the rate-limiter attribution layer after the orchestrator change. Evidence: spike in small GETs coincident with 429 wave; token refill metric for tenant shows rapid drain during same window.
What we looked at:
- Ingress traces (edge -> auth -> rate-limiter) show healthcheck requests carrying same api-key header as workers (ephemeral agents reuse short-lived credentials).
- Rate-limiter bucket metrics: tenant_token_count dropped to zero at 17:21:05Z; refill rate unchanged.
- Orchestrator telemetry: orchestrator introduced a pooling optimization that increases heartbeat frequency to 1s under high fanout.
- No changes in billing/credits that would cause depletion.
Interim conclusion: combination of short-lived credentials + increased heartbeat frequency produced a burst of token accounting events that the rate-limiter counted against tenant quota, leading to background ingest 429s. Interactive routes were on higher-priority lane and preserved.
customer_updates:
2026-03-12 18:00 UTC - Support: Thanks for the report — we see the same spikes and are investigating. Could you confirm whether your workers and sidecar share the same API key or use separate service accounts?
2026-03-12 18:15 UTC - AtlasData: Workers use the same service account; orchestrator creates ephemeral processes that use short-lived tokens minted from the same account.
2026-03-13 09:30 UTC - Support: We've identified a likely accounting skew; working on a mitigation and will follow up with a patch timeline.
2026-03-14 14:10 UTC - Support: Rolling a config change to isolate healthchecks from tenant quota in staging for validation.
comments:
Support (Carlos): Added initial triage, flagged to infra-sre.
Infra-SRE (Leah O'Connor): Reproduced locally with orchestrator v2.3.4; heap of 1s heartbeats causes ~2.5x token-cost due to our pre-auth path incrementing token counters on connection accept.
Engineer (Mason Liu): Proposed quick mitigation: whitelist /health and /metrics paths from tenant token accounting when requests originate from ephemeral pool IP range OR when X-Worker-Role header present.
Support (Carlos): Customer confirmed ephemeral agents all run from the same subnet (10.2.34.0/24) in their private VPC. Will attempt subnet-based temporary exclusion as workaround.
proposed_workaround: Short-term workaround applied (2026-03-14 02:00 UTC): exclude /health and /metrics requests from tenant token decrement when source IP is in AtlasData ephemeral subnet (10.2.34.0/24). Result: 429 waves stopped in observed window for subsequent bulk runs. Workaround details: edge rule change + rate-limiter flag 'exclude_health_from_quota' enabled for tenant. Note: this is a scoped workaround and not enabled globally.
resolution_notes:
Fix deployed (2026-03-14 13:45 UTC): rate-limiter change to attribution logic so that requests tagged with X-Ephemeral-Worker:true OR matching configured ephemeral-subnet do not decrement tenant token bucket for healthcheck-like endpoints. CAVEATS: requests must still pass auth and not be used for requests that should be metered; updated docs and added a safety check to ensure POST/PUT on non-excluded paths never bypass quota.
Related PRs: redwood/ingest-orchestrator#1128 (orchestrator opt-out header), redwood/rate-limiter#439 (attribution fix).
Follow-ups:
- Engineering task created to add a validation check to ensure ephemeral worker token paths are explicit (INT-3301).
- Add guidance to dedicated onboarding docs about separating service accounts for ephemeral processes vs long-running workers (confluence.redwood/KB/tenant-rate-accounting).
- Recommend customer to rotate the service account and, optionally, issue dedicated ephemeral credentials with narrower scope.
next_steps:
1) Close support ticket after customer verifies no residual 429s in their next 48h bulk run.
2) Postmortem-lite: summarize root cause and mitigation, add to runbook.
3) Long-term: introduce a dedicated ephemeral credential flow and document recommended orchestration config.
resolution_status: Fix deployed to prod; customer workaround validated in tenant; awaiting 48h stability window before closing.
